summary.lead: Official summary (Congressional Research Service, Introduced in House):

blocks.text: This bill allows a veteran with a combat-related disability to receive retirement pay, without reduction, concurrently with their disability compensation. This includes veterans with a combat-related disability and fewer than 20 years of creditable service. (Currently, veterans who receive combat-related special compensation and retirement pay are subject to an offset in retirement pay for concurrent receipt of such benefits.)

This measure would let a veteran who has a combat-related disability receive their retirement pay in full, at the same time as their disability compensation. The rule also covers veterans who have a combat-related disability and fewer than 20 years of creditable service. Under current rules, veterans who receive combat-related special compensation along with retirement pay have their retirement pay reduced because they are getting both benefits.
